findings.location: content.body.variantPolicyUk: «Le для предметів і для жінок не приймаємо»
findings.description: The blanket rejection for women excludes accepted courtesy leísmo when addressing a woman as «usted». This falls within the skill's explicit address-form scope. The ordinary third-person feminine case and courtesy address require different treatment.
findings.suggestion: Keep «la» as the feminine model, but distinguish ordinary third-person reference from accepted courtesy «le». Resolve the pending plural policy separately, distinguishing ordinary third-person «los» from courtesy «les».

items.reviewerAnswer: Use «lo, la, los, las» according to gender and number. Singular masculine personal «le» is also standard; courtesy «le/les» can address women as well.
items.notes: The singular masculine «lo/le» policy is otherwise sound.
sources: RAE/ASALE, Diccionario panhispánico de dudas, «leísmo», discussion of leísmo de cortesía with «usted/ustedes» (from memory).
Packet: content.body.scope.noteUk explicitly includes address using «usted» and «ustedes».

findings.description: The example is correct, but the unqualified instruction omits personal «a», required with a specific human direct object such as Ana. This is particularly misleading in a lesson that also uses «buscar» with people.
findings.suggestion: Restrict the no-preposition statement to the inanimate example and add a contrasting personal example: «Busco las llaves» / «Busco a Ana».

items.reviewerAnswer: «buscar» means «шукати»: «Busco las llaves», but «Busco a Ana» for a specific person.
sources: RAE/ASALE, Diccionario panhispánico de dudas, «a», personal «a» before definite human direct objects (from memory).

findings.location: content.body.steps[id=s3].blocks[3].text: «Ми вчимо lo; про предмети і про жінок le не вживаємо.»
findings.description: The unrestricted ban on «le» for women excludes accepted courtesy address to a woman using «usted». The same explanation explicitly introduces address forms through «¿La ayudo, señora?».
findings.suggestion: Distinguish ordinary third-person feminine reference from courtesy address. Keep «la» as the teaching model without declaring courtesy «le» incorrect.

items.reviewerAnswer: Appropriate models include «Ana me llama», «¿La leche? La compro» and «No las veo». Ordinary feminine reference uses «la/las», while courtesy address can also use «le/les».
sources: RAE/ASALE, Diccionario panhispánico de dudas, «leísmo», discussion of leísmo de cortesía (from memory).
Packet: content.body.steps[id=s3].blocks[0] includes «¿La ayudo, señora?».

findings.location: task.hints[0].blocks[1].text: «Про предмети і про жінок — лише lo, la.»
findings.description: The unrestricted statement omits plural «los/las» and excludes accepted courtesy «le» for a woman addressed as «usted». The answer key for Pablo itself correctly accepts «lo» and «le».
findings.suggestion: Describe ordinary third-person forms as «lo, la, los, las», with gender and number agreement. Distinguish singular masculine personal «le» and courtesy address instead of giving a blanket prohibition.

items.reviewerAnswer: «lo» fits the listed four-form instruction; «le» is also standard Spain Spanish for Pablo.
items.notes: The prompt could also explicitly acknowledge the accepted «le» variant.
sources: RAE/ASALE, Diccionario panhispánico de dudas, «pronombres personales átonos», third-person accusative forms (from memory).

findings.location: task.hints[0].blocks[1].text: «Про предмети і про жінок — лише lo, la.»
findings.description: The hint excludes plural forms even though this task requires «las». Its blanket restriction also fails to distinguish ordinary feminine reference from accepted courtesy «le/les». The option key for «mis hermanas» is correct.
findings.suggestion: Include «los/las» in the general rule and distinguish ordinary third-person reference from courtesy address. Retain «las» as the answer here.

findings.location: task.hints[0].blocks[1].text: «Про предмети і про жінок — лише lo, la.»
findings.description: The general hint omits plural «los/las» and incorrectly rules out courtesy «le» for female «usted». Neither issue changes the correct answer «lo» for «el ordenador».
findings.suggestion: State the ordinary four-form paradigm with gender and number agreement, then distinguish singular masculine personal «le» and courtesy address.

items.notes: Calling the specified laptop «el ordenador» is acceptable; it does not need to be changed to assess this pronoun.

findings.description: The question already contains the object pronoun «me», not an object noun. The required operation is changing speaker perspective from «me» to «te», so the instruction describes the wrong operation.
findings.suggestion: Ask learners to answer using the appropriate pronoun, or explicitly explain that the pronoun changes with the speaker.

items.reviewerAnswer: «te llamo»; «yo te llamo» and «te llamo yo» also fit the blank.
items.notes: The Spanish model and reviewed answers are otherwise correct; the open key permits additional answers to remain unresolved.
sources: Packet: task.prompt[2] is «—¿Me llamas mañana? —Sí, ___ mañana.»; its object is already «me».

findings.location: task.prompt[0]: «Дайте відповідь, замінивши іменник займенником.»; task.errors[2]: «les espero» marked incorrect
findings.description: The object «nos» is already a pronoun, so no object noun can be replaced. Separately, rejecting «les espero» assumes a «vosotros» reply, although the prompt does not establish how the respondent addresses the group.
findings.suggestion: Describe the change of speaker perspective and explicitly establish that the reply addresses the group as «vosotros». Otherwise resolve the courtesy «ustedes» reading before grading «les espero» incorrect.

items.reviewerAnswer: «os espero» for informal plural address. Courtesy «les espero» is possible if the reply addresses the group as «ustedes».
items.notes: The instruction mismatch is definite. The treatment of «les espero» is independently underdetermined, not a claim that «les» is correct for «vosotros».
sources: Packet: task.prompt[1] is «—¿Nos esperas en el parque? —Sí, ___ allí.».

findings.description: The question contains the object pronoun «me», not an object noun. The answer changes the pronoun's person with the speaker.
findings.suggestion: Ask for a reply using the appropriate pronoun, rather than instructing the learner to replace a noun.

items.reviewerAnswer: «te busco», «te busco yo» or «yo te busco».
items.notes: The Spanish answers and per-target error outcomes are otherwise consistent.

findings.description: The object in «¿Nos invitas a cenar?» is already the pronoun «nos». The answer changes speaker perspective; it does not replace an object noun.
findings.suggestion: Ask learners to answer using the appropriate pronoun, or describe the speaker-dependent change from «nos» to «os».

items.reviewerAnswer: «os invito», «os invito yo» or «yo os invito».
sources: Packet: task.prompt[1] is «—¿Nos invitas a cenar? —Claro, ___ el sábado.».

findings.description: The object is already «nos». «Profesora» is a vocative, not the noun that should be replaced. The instruction therefore describes an operation that does not match the dialogue.
findings.suggestion: Ask for a reply using the appropriate pronoun. If «os» is specifically required, establish that the teacher addresses the learners as «vosotros».

items.reviewerAnswer: «os ayudo» fits an informal plural classroom reply. Formal «ustedes» could instead produce «los/las ayudo» or courtesy «les ayudo».
items.notes: The open key does not automatically reject unreviewed formal-address variants.

findings.location: task.prompt[1]: «no / lo / compro»; task.closed=true with only «No lo compro.» accepted
findings.description: The visible instruction does not specify that «no» must negate the verb. The negative-clause reading and an initial negative response followed by an affirmative clause permit different punctuation and meaning. The optional translation hint selects the negative reading, but the bare prompt does not.
findings.suggestion: Explicitly request a negative declarative sentence, or supply context establishing the function of «no» before applying the closed key.

items.reviewerAnswer: «No lo compro.» as a negative statement; «No, lo compro.» is possible with «no» as a separate negative response.
items.notes: The accepted negative sentence itself is correct.
sources: Course contract rule 3: a closed key must cover answers correct for the stated context.
Course contract rule 5: internal punctuation is not normalized.
RAE/ASALE, Diccionario panhispánico de dudas, «coma», separation of initial affirmative/negative response particles (from memory).

findings.location: task.prompt[1]: «no / la / veo»; task.closed=true with only «No la veo.» accepted
findings.description: The visible prompt leaves the function of «no» unspecified. Clausal negation gives the accepted sentence; a separate negative response permits «No, la veo». The translation hint reveals the intended negative meaning, but this constraint is absent from the initial instruction.
findings.suggestion: Request a negative declarative sentence explicitly, or add context that resolves the two readings.

items.reviewerAnswer: «No la veo.» as a negative statement; «No, la veo.» is possible as a negative response followed by an affirmative clause.
items.notes: There is no error in the accepted negative word order.
sources: Course contract rules 3 and 5.
RAE/ASALE, Diccionario panhispánico de dudas, «coma», separation of initial affirmative/negative response particles (from memory).

findings.location: task.prompt[1]: «no / os / espero»; task.closed=true with only «No os espero.» accepted
findings.description: The visible prompt does not distinguish verbal negation from a separate response «no». Both arrangements preserve correct pronoun placement, but differ in meaning and internal punctuation. Only the optional translation hint establishes the intended negative reading.
findings.suggestion: Explicitly require a negative declarative sentence, or supply a context fixing the function of «no».

items.reviewerAnswer: «No os espero.» as a negative statement; «No, os espero.» is possible as a negative response followed by an affirmative clause.
items.notes: The supplied negative answer is correct under the intended reading.
sources: Course contract rules 3 and 5.
RAE/ASALE, Diccionario panhispánico de dudas, «coma», separation of initial affirmative/negative response particles (from memory).

findings.location: task.prompt[1]: «no / te / entiendo»; task.closed=true with only «No te entiendo.» accepted
findings.description: The visible instruction does not specify whether «no» negates «entiendo» or serves as a separate response. These readings produce different valid sentences. The translation hint identifies the intended negative meaning, but the initial prompt does not constrain it.
findings.suggestion: Explicitly request a negative declarative sentence, or add context resolving the function of «no» before retaining the closed key.

items.reviewerAnswer: «No te entiendo.» as a negative statement; «No, te entiendo.» is possible as a negative response followed by an affirmative clause.
items.notes: The accepted negative sentence is correct.
